examples.ko: 월요일 아침이면 동료들끼리 서로 푸념하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: On Monday mornings, coworkers often grumble to each other.

examples.ko: 아이는 숙제가 너무 많다고 푸념하면서도 책상 앞에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The child grumbled that there was too much homework, but still sat down at the desk.

examples.ko: 친구가 요즘 회사가 힘들다고 계속 푸념해요.
examples.en: My friend keeps complaining that work is tough these days.

examples.ko: 그만 푸념하고 이제 같이 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's stop grumbling and look for a solution together.
Grandfather sometimes complains that his back hurts.

examples.ko: 퇴근길에 남편이 상사 때문에 힘들다고 푸념했어요.
examples.en: On the way home from work, my husband grumbled about how hard his boss makes things.

explain: '불평하다'가 마음에 안 드는 점을 따지는 느낌이라면, '푸념하다'는 힘들고 답답한 마음을 그냥 털어놓는 느낌이에요. 해결해 달라는 말보다는 하소연에 가까워서 듣는 사람도 '그렇구나' 하고 들어 주면 돼요. '푸념을 늘어놓다', '푸념을 하다'처럼 명사 '푸념'과 함께도 자주 써요.
explain_en: While '불평하다' sounds like pointing out what you dislike, '푸념하다' means venting tired or frustrated feelings. It is closer to pouring out your troubles than demanding a fix, so the listener can just nod along. It is also often used with the noun, as in '푸념을 늘어놓다' or '푸념을 하다'.

examples.ko: 손님을 푸대접하는 가게는 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: A shop that treats its customers poorly won't last long.
Please don't treat people badly just because they are new.
Even though it's a country restaurant, they don't treat guests poorly.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 혼자 온 손님을 푸대접해서 다시 안 가요.
examples.en: That restaurant treats solo diners badly, so I don't go back.

examples.ko: 가족이라고 해서 푸대접해도 되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being family doesn't mean you can treat them badly.

examples.ko: 그분은 어려운 사람들을 절대 푸대접하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He never treated people in need with disrespect.

explain: 반대말은 '극진히 대접하다'예요. 비슷한 말 '홀대하다'는 조금 더 글에서 많이 보여요. 명사 '푸대접'과 함께 '푸대접을 받다'라고 하면 '대우를 못 받다'라는 말이 돼요.
explain_en: The opposite is '극진히 대접하다' (to treat with great hospitality). A similar word, '홀대하다', appears a bit more in writing. With the noun, '푸대접을 받다' means to be treated poorly.

en: with a flap; with a flutter

examples.en: A pigeon flew up with a flap of its wings.
The chicken ran off, flapping noisily.
A bird hit the window and fluttered down.

examples.ko: 갑자기 푸드덕 하는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a sudden flapping sound.
A pheasant burst up from the grass with a flutter.

examples.ko: 참새 한 마리가 푸드덕 하고 나뭇가지에서 날아갔어요.
examples.en: A sparrow flapped off the branch.

explain: 새나 닭이 날개를 힘차게 한 번 칠 때 나는 소리와 모습이에요. 계속 반복될 때는 '푸드덕푸드덕'이라고 하고, 동사 '푸드덕거리다'도 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '퍼덕', '파닥'도 있는데 날개를 치는 크기와 세기에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and look of a bird or chicken beating its wings once, hard. For repeated flapping, say '푸드덕푸드덕', and there is also the verb '푸드덕거리다'. Similar words like '퍼덕' and '파닥' differ in the size and strength of the flapping.

examples.en: The chickens are flapping around in the coop.
The bird got caught in the net and kept flapping.

examples.ko: 창문 밖에서 새가 푸드덕거리는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear a bird fluttering outside the window.
The pigeon splashed water, flapping its wings.
The bird that had been flapping for a while finally took off.

examples.ko: 새장 속 앵무새가 밤새 푸드덕거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The parrot in the cage flapped all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 날개를 계속 치는 모습에 써요. 주로 새, 닭 같은 날짐승이 주어예요. 한 번 치는 소리는 부사 '푸드덕'을 쓰고, 계속될 때 '푸드덕거리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for wings that keep beating, mostly with birds and poultry as the subject. For a single flap use the adverb '푸드덕', and for continued flapping use '푸드덕거리다'.

examples.en: Fresh green sprouts have come up in the flower bed.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 잔디가 푸릇푸릇 살아났어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the lawn came back to fresh green life.

examples.ko: 봄이 되자 들판이 푸릇푸릇 물들기 시작했어요.
examples.en: With spring, the fields began to turn fresh green.

examples.ko: 창가 화분의 파가 푸릇푸릇 자라고 있어요.
examples.en: The green onion in the pot by the window is growing fresh and green.

examples.ko: 푸릇푸릇 돋은 풀을 보니 봄이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the grass sprouting green, it feels like spring has come.

examples.ko: 논에 모가 푸릇푸릇 자라서 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: The rice seedlings are growing green in the paddy, and it looks nice.

explain: 새싹, 풀, 잎처럼 막 자란 식물이 싱그럽게 푸른 모양이에요. '파릇파릇'보다 조금 더 짙고 큰 느낌이에요. 봄 풍경에 잘 어울리고 '푸릇푸릇하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes newly grown plants such as sprouts, grass and leaves in a fresh, lively green. It feels a little deeper and larger than '파릇파릇'. It suits spring scenery and also works as '푸릇푸릇하다'.

examples.en: The lawn in the yard is fresh and green.
In spring the mountains turn fresh green, and it lifts my mood.
Fresh green sprouts came up in the pot.

examples.ko: 비가 오고 나니 나뭇잎이 더 푸릇푸릇해 보여요.
examples.en: After the rain, the leaves look even fresher and greener.
The market is full of fresh green vegetables.

examples.ko: 푸릇푸릇하던 들판이 가을이 되자 노랗게 변했어요.
examples.en: The fields that had been fresh green turned yellow in autumn.

explain: '푸르다'보다 막 돋아난 풀이나 잎의 싱싱한 초록빛에 잘 어울려요. 새싹, 잔디, 채소처럼 어리고 생기 있는 식물에 써요. 가을에 노랗게 변하기 전의 모습은 '푸릇푸릇하던 들판'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '푸르다', it fits the fresh green of newly sprouted grass and leaves. It is used for young, lively plants such as sprouts, lawns and vegetables. A field before it turns yellow in autumn is '푸릇푸릇하던 들판'.

examples.ko: 며칠 잠을 못 자서 얼굴이 푸석푸석 부었어요.
examples.en: After days without sleep, my face is puffy.
My hair is dry and brittle.
The stale bread crumbled dryly.
It's winter, so my skin has become dry and dull.
The dry soil crumbled and scattered.
The rice cooled and went dry and hard.

explain: 윤기와 물기가 없어서 거칠고 부서질 듯한 모습, 또는 피곤해서 얼굴이 부은 모습에 써요. 머리카락, 피부, 빵, 흙처럼 촉촉해야 할 것이 말랐을 때 자주 나와요. 형용사 '푸석푸석하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes things that lack moisture and shine, looking rough and ready to crumble, or a face puffy from tiredness. It often comes up when something that should be moist is dry, such as hair, skin, bread or soil. It also works as the adjective '푸석푸석하다'.

examples.en: I didn't sleep, so my face looks puffy and dull.
My hair is dry and frizzy, so I wore a hat today.
A moisturizing cream is good for dull, dry skin.
You look puffy-faced lately because you're tired.
The old cookie is dry and tastes bad.
My dry hair became soft after some care.

explain: 윤기 없이 메마르고 거칠어 보일 때 써요. 피곤한 얼굴, 머리카락, 피부에 자주 쓰고 물기 없는 빵이나 과자에도 써요. '촉촉하다'의 반대 느낌이고, 얼굴이 부어 보일 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes things that look dry, dull and rough without shine. It is common for a tired face, hair and skin, and also for dry bread or cookies. It is the opposite of '촉촉하다', and it can also describe a puffy-looking face.

examples.ko: 텃밭에서 푸성귀를 뜯어 와서 쌈을 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I picked greens from the garden and ate them as wraps.

examples.ko: 할머니가 시골에서 푸성귀를 한 보따리 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sent a big bundle of greens from the countryside.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁은 푸성귀 위주로 간단히 먹을게요.
examples.en: For dinner tonight I'll eat simply, mostly greens.

examples.ko: 여름에는 푸성귀가 흔해서 반찬값이 덜 들어요.
examples.en: Greens are plentiful in summer, so side dishes cost less.
I bought fresh greens cheaply at the market.
Rice tastes good with just some greens.

explain: '채소'보다 상추, 쑥갓 같은 잎채소나 텃밭에서 기른 푸른 채소의 느낌이 강해요. 마트 진열대보다는 시골 밥상이나 집밥 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 일상에서는 그냥 '채소'라고 말하는 사람이 더 많아요.
explain_en: Compared with '채소', it leans toward leafy greens like lettuce and crown daisy, or green vegetables grown in a home garden. It suits talk of country meals and home cooking more than supermarket shelves. In daily speech, many people simply say '채소'.

examples.en: The boarding house I found was the back part of a butcher's shop.
In the old days, every neighborhood had a butcher's shop.

examples.ko: 할머니는 푸줏간에서 고기를 한 근 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother bought a pound of meat at the butcher's.

examples.ko: 푸줏간 아저씨가 고기를 두툼하게 썰어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The butcher cut the meat thick for me.

examples.ko: 요즘은 푸줏간 대신 마트에서 고기를 사요.
examples.en: These days I buy meat at the supermarket instead of a butcher's.

examples.ko: 푸줏간 앞을 지나가면 고기 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: Passing in front of the butcher's, I smelled meat.

explain: 요즘 가게 이름이나 말로는 '정육점'을 더 많이 써요. '푸줏간'은 옛날 느낌이 있어서 드라마나 소설, 어른들 말씀에서 자주 들어요. 고기를 파는 가게라는 점은 같아요.
explain_en: Today '정육점' is more common as a shop name or word. '푸줏간' has an old-fashioned feel and is often heard in dramas, novels and from older people. Both are shops that sell meat.

examples.en: A lavish feast table was laid out.
Today I ate plenty of meat.
It's a holiday, so the food is really plentiful.

examples.ko: 푸진 상을 받으니 부자가 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: Getting such a generous spread makes me feel rich.
Grandmother entertained the guests generously.
The table was so full that I couldn't finish it all.

explain: 주로 음식이나 상차림이 넉넉하고 풍성할 때 써요. 일상에서는 비슷한 '푸짐하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '푸지다'는 '푸지게 먹다'처럼 부사형으로 자주 나와요. '푸지어'가 줄어서 '푸져요'가 되는 점도 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when food or a table spread is generous and rich. In daily speech the similar '푸짐하다' is more common, and '푸지다' often shows up in the adverbial form, as in '푸지게 먹다'. Note that '푸지어' contracts to '푸져요'.

examples.ko: 이 원피스는 풀빛이라서 봄에 입기 좋아요.
examples.en: This dress is grass green, so it's nice to wear in spring.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 산이 풀빛으로 반짝였어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the mountain sparkled in grass green.
I'd like to buy a grass-green sweater.
I painted the wall grass green, and the room got brighter.
The child drew a tree with a grass-green crayon.
The lake water has a grass-green tint.

explain: '초록색'이나 '연두색'보다 풀잎에서 느껴지는 싱그러운 초록이라는 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '초록색'을 더 많이 쓰고, '풀빛'은 글이나 감성적인 표현에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '초록색' or '연두색', it carries the feel of the fresh green of grass blades. In everyday talk '초록색' is more common, while '풀빛' suits writing and more poetic expressions.

en: with a plop; with a thud

examples.en: I was so tired that I plopped down on the sofa.
When the pole broke, the tent collapsed with a thump.
As soon as I got home, I flopped onto the bed.
When the car passed, a puff of dust rose.
Hearing the news, Mother sank to the floor.

examples.ko: 다리에 힘이 풀려서 바닥에 풀썩 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: My legs gave out and I dropped to the floor.

explain: 힘이 빠져서 갑자기 주저앉거나 눕는 모습, 또는 먼지가 한꺼번에 일어나는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 '털썩'은 더 묵직하게 떨어지는 느낌이 있어요. '풀썩 앉다', '풀썩 주저앉다'처럼 동작을 나타내는 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes suddenly sinking down or lying down as strength drains away, or dust puffing up all at once. The similar '털썩' feels heavier. It pairs with action verbs, as in '풀썩 앉다' and '풀썩 주저앉다'.

examples.en: I spread glue on the back of the paper and stuck it on the wall.
I helped apply glue to the envelope flap.
Apply paste to the edge of the wallpaper and stick it on slowly.
The child's hands got sticky from gluing the drawing paper.

examples.ko: 풀칠한 자리가 마르면 다시 눌러 주세요.
examples.en: When the glued spot dries, press it down again.

examples.ko: 하루 벌어 하루 먹으며 겨우 입에 풀칠해요.
examples.en: I earn day to day and barely get by.

explain: 종이나 천에 풀을 바르는 일이에요. 막대풀로 붙일 때는 '풀로 붙이다'라고도 많이 말해요. '입에 풀칠하다'는 겨우 먹고산다는 비유로 써요.

phrases.example: 일자리가 없어서 겨우 입에 풀칠하며 살았어요.
phrases.en: I had no job, so I barely managed to get by.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨우 굶지 않을 만큼만 먹고사는 가난한 형편을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes living so poorly that you can barely afford enough to eat.

explain_en: It means spreading paste on paper or cloth. When using a glue stick, people also often say '풀로 붙이다'. '입에 풀칠하다' is a figurative expression for barely making a living.

examples.en: Dust was blowing around, so I closed the window.
Steam is rising from the pot.
It was a day when snow was fluttering through the air.

examples.ko: 차가 지나갈 때마다 흙먼지가 풀풀 일어요.
examples.en: Every time a car passes, dust kicks up.

examples.ko: 라면 냄새가 풀풀 풍겨서 배가 고파졌어요.
examples.en: The smell of ramen wafted over and made me hungry.
Autumn leaves are fluttering in the wind.

explain: 먼지, 눈, 김, 연기처럼 가벼운 것이 날리거나 피어오를 때, 또 냄새가 퍼질 때 써요. '먼지가 풀풀 날리다', '냄새가 풀풀 나다'처럼 자주 쓰는 짝이 있어요. '폴폴'보다 조금 더 크고 거센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes light things such as dust, snow, steam and smoke drifting or rising, and smells spreading. Common pairs are '먼지가 풀풀 날리다' and '냄새가 풀풀 나다'. It feels a little bigger and stronger than '폴폴'.

examples.en: The mask shortage continued for a while.
It's a popular item, so it's in short supply online.
Prices rose a lot due to the shortage of farm produce.
The new product became scarce as soon as it came out.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 채소 품귀 현상이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, a vegetable shortage occurred.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 과자는 품귀라서 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: This snack is in short supply these days, so it's hard to find.

explain: 가게 한 곳에서 물건이 다 팔린 '품절'과 달리, 시장 전체에 물건이 모자라 구하기 어려운 상태를 말해요. 뉴스에서 '품귀 현상'이라는 말로 자주 나와요. 반대로 물건이 넘치는 상태는 '과잉', '넘쳐 나다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike '품절' (sold out at one shop), it means goods are scarce across the whole market and hard to get. It appears often in the news as '품귀 현상'. The opposite, an oversupply, is described with '과잉' or '넘쳐 나다'.

examples.en: In the old days, neighbors planted rice together by taking turns helping.

examples.ko: 이번 이사는 친구들과 품앗이하듯 서로 도왔어요.
examples.en: For this move, friends helped each other like a work exchange.

examples.ko: 품앗이는 농사철에 서로 일손을 빌려주던 방법이에요.
examples.en: Pumasi was a way of lending each other a hand in farming season.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 엄마들은 육아 품앗이를 해요.
examples.en: The mothers in our neighborhood do a childcare exchange.

examples.ko: 김장은 이웃과 품앗이로 하면 훨씬 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: Kimchi-making finishes much faster when done as a neighborly work exchange.

examples.ko: 오늘 도와줬으니 다음엔 네가 와 줘요. 품앗이잖아요!
examples.en: I helped today, so you come next time. It's a work exchange, after all!

explain: 개인과 개인이 일손을 주고받는 전통이에요. 마을 사람 모두가 함께 일하는 '두레'와 달라요. 요즘에는 '육아 품앗이'처럼 서로 도움을 주고받는 일에 비유해서 써요.
explain_en: It is a tradition in which individuals exchange labor with each other. It differs from '두레', where the whole village works together. Today it is used figuratively for mutual help, as in '육아 품앗이' (childcare exchange).

examples.en: The neighbors helped each other and finished making kimchi.
We agreed to take turns helping each other move.
In farming season, neighbors swapping work was a common sight.

examples.ko: 아이 돌봄을 품앗이하면 서로 부담이 줄어요.
examples.en: If we take turns minding the kids, the burden is lighter for everyone.

examples.ko: 친구랑 번갈아 숙제를 도와주며 품앗이하는 셈이에요.
examples.en: My friend and I take turns helping with homework, so it's a kind of exchange.
The villagers gathered and took turns helping build the house.

explain: 서로 번갈아 일을 도와주고 받는다는 점이 핵심이라서, 한쪽만 돕는 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 옛날 농촌 이야기뿐 아니라 요즘 이웃끼리 돌봄이나 일을 나눌 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: The key idea is taking turns helping and being helped, so it doesn't fit one-sided help. Besides old farming stories, it is used figuratively today when neighbors share care or chores.

examples.en: My friends critiqued each other's drawings.
The judge commented on each entry one by one.

examples.ko: 영화를 보고 나와서 장면을 품평하는 게 취미예요.
examples.en: My hobby is commenting on scenes after coming out of a movie.

examples.ko: 남의 외모를 함부로 품평하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't carelessly comment on other people's looks.
I went to a gathering where people critique the taste of coffee.

examples.ko: 선생님이 작품을 품평한 뒤 점수를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: After critiquing the works, the teacher told us the scores.

explain: '평가하다'보다 물건이나 작품의 좋고 나쁜 점을 하나하나 따져 말하는 느낌이 있어요. 음식, 그림, 영화처럼 취향이 있는 대상에 잘 쓰여요. 사람의 외모나 모습에 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '평가하다', it feels like going through the good and bad points of a product or work one by one. It suits things of taste such as food, art and films. Using it for a person's looks can sound rude.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 특산물 품평회가 다음 주에 열려요.
examples.en: A local specialty products show is being held next week.
I went to a new strawberry variety tasting show.
At the show, the judges gave scores.

examples.ko: 농가들이 올해 수확한 사과를 품평회에 내놓았어요.
examples.en: Farms entered this year's harvested apples in the show.

examples.ko: 신제품 품평회라서 회사 사람들이 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: It was a new product review, so everyone in the company gathered.

examples.ko: 이 쌀은 지난 품평회에서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: This rice won a prize at the last show.

explain: 박람회나 전시회가 구경하는 데 중심이 있다면, '품평회'는 물건의 품질을 비교하고 평가하는 데 중심이 있어요. 농산물, 신제품, 식품 등에서 자주 나와요. 지역 소식이나 뉴스에서도 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: While an expo or exhibition focuses on viewing, a '품평회' focuses on comparing and judging product quality. It appears often for farm produce, new products and food. You can also see it in local news.

examples.en: I'm still a rookie who isn't good at the job yet.
I made a lot of mistakes when I was a newbie.

examples.ko: 풋내기라고 해도 열정은 누구에게도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even though I'm a novice, I'm second to none in passion.
Though a rookie, the player stayed calm in the game.
A greenhorn reporter landed a big scoop.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 풋내기들이 많아서 분위기가 밝아요.
examples.en: Our team has many newcomers, so the mood is bright.

explain: '초보자'보다 경험이 적고 서툴러 보이는 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서, 남이 말하면 얕잡아 보는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 자기 자신을 낮춰 말할 때는 괜찮아요. 중립적으로 말하려면 '초보', '신입'을 쓰세요.
explain_en: Compared with '초보자', it suggests someone with little experience who looks unskilled, so it can sound belittling when others say it. It is fine for describing yourself modestly. For a neutral tone, use '초보' or '신입'.

examples.en: My crush in middle school was puppy love.
I still remember the flutter of that puppy love.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으면 풋사랑 시절이 떠올라요.
examples.en: Hearing that song reminds me of my puppy-love days.
It was closer to puppy love than real love.

examples.ko: 소설 속 두 주인공의 풋사랑이 귀여워요.
examples.en: The two main characters' puppy love in the novel is cute.

examples.ko: 풋사랑은 대부분 오래가지 못하지만 추억으로 남아요.
examples.en: Puppy love mostly doesn't last, but it stays as a memory.

explain: '첫사랑'이 처음 한 사랑이라면, '풋사랑'은 어리고 서툴러서 덜 익은 사랑이라는 느낌이에요. '풋-'은 덜 익은 것에 붙는 말이라서 '풋과일'처럼도 써요. 보통 지난 일을 돌아보며 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: While '첫사랑' is your first love, '풋사랑' suggests an immature, unripe love of young people. The prefix '풋-' attaches to unripe things, as in '풋과일'. It is mostly used when looking back on the past.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 보는 풍광이 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: The view from the mountaintop is really magnificent.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 바다 풍광이 좋기로 유명해요.
examples.en: This cafe is famous for its good sea views.
I'm captivated by Jeju's scenery, so I go often.
I drank tea while looking at the scenery outside the window.
Photographers gathered to capture the autumn scenery.
Thanks to the beautiful scenery, the trip was enjoyable.

explain: '풍경'이 눈에 보이는 장면 전반을 가리킨다면, '풍광'은 자연의 아름다운 경치라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 대화보다는 여행 소개, 방송, 글에서 자주 보여요. '풍광이 좋다', '빼어난 풍광'처럼 써요.
explain_en: While '풍경' refers to any scene you see, '풍광' leans more toward beautiful natural scenery. It appears more in travel introductions, broadcasts and writing than in conversation. Typical uses are '풍광이 좋다' and '빼어난 풍광'.
